#213848. Tech Report: 5 questions to ask before you tap ‘invest’ on real estate apps

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1075 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 5 questions to ask before you tap ‘invest’ on real estate apps

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, real estate investing apps show the average return first.
  • Investing in real estate used to mean buying a building.
  • Industry observers note that access is a good thing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, real estate investing apps show the average return first. Amanda Neely, CFP, shares five questions on fees, payouts, liquidity and more.

Investing in real estate used to mean buying a building. Now it can mean tapping a button. Crowdfunding platforms, fractional-ownership apps and private lending marketplaces let you put $500 or $50,000 into real estate without ever signing a deed. Plenty of agents use them for their own money, and clients ask agents about them too.

Industry observers note that access is a good thing. But the app puts the friendliest number front and center … an average rate of return. It rarely demonstrates you your actual annualized return after fees and defaults or how far your balance could drop in a bad year.

Sources indicate that this fall, I sat down with several people who had all invested through the same program. Each of them had a different understanding of where their money was going.

One had stopped going to the program’s update calls years ago, because nobody on them would tell her whether she was making money or losing it. Every one of them could tell me, to the dollar, what landed in their account each month.

I haven’t put my own money into these platforms, and most of the reasons why are on this list.

Here are five questions to ask before you, or a client, put money into any real estate investing platform.

It has been revealed that some platforms are marketplaces. They connect you to deals that someone else runs. Others steer your money into funds they manage themselves. The second setup isn’t automatically bad, but it means the company can get paid more than once: a platform or membership fee up front, then a management fee inside the fund.

Recent findings suggest that how to check: Find the fund’s name on your statement and look up who manages it. If it’s the same manufacturer that recommended it (or a close affiliate), ask for every layer of fees in writing.

Real estate funds on these platforms usually pay monthly or quarterly distributions, and part of each payment is often classified as return of capital. In plain English, part of what you’re paid is your own money coming back.

Industry observers note that in real estate, some return of capital is normal. Depreciation lets a property fund pay out cash that isn’t taxed as income yet, and that gets labeled return of capital, too. The warning sign is return of capital paired with a sliding share value.

Recent findings suggest that if the distributions hold steady while the fund’s value per share (often called NAV) keeps dropping, the income is coming out of your principal. You still feel paid every month, and the account is getting smaller.

How to check: In the app, compare the fund’s value per share on the day you bought with today’s. Then look at your year-end tax forms, which show return of capital separately from dividends.

In a recent development, say you put $20,000 into a private loan that pays you $400 a month for five years. That’s $24,000 back. Spread over five years, it looks like about 4 percent a year. But because part of every payment is your own principal coming home, the annualized return is actually closer to 7.4 percent. The payout made it look worse than it was.

Sources indicate that now flip it. That 7.4 percent only holds if the borrower pays every month. Lending platforms spread your money across many borrowers, and some of them won’t pay. A platform advertising 10 percent that loses 4 percent of its loans to default each year is paying you closer to 6 percent.

How to check: Ask the platform for the annualized return after fees and defaults, not the payout rate. Then ask what that number was in its worst year.

Many of these platforms are newer than the last real estate downturn. A platform that developed when money was cheap hasn’t shown you how it behaves when money is expensive. The firm running the app is also a business, and businesses fail. WeWork, the shared-office company, was valued at $47 billion in 2019 and filed for bankruptcy in November 2023.

How to check: Find the platform’s launch date and look for at least one stretch of rising rates or falling prices in its history. Then ask where your investment actually sits. Many platforms hold each property or fund in its own legal entity, separate from the manufacturer itself, so your share can survive if the platform doesn’t. If neither answer is clear, size your investment like the experiment it is.

Many platforms expect you to stay in for five years or more. Some charge a penalty to leave early, others limit how much can come out each quarter, and many reserve the right to pause withdrawals entirely. In spring 2020, Fundrise, one of the best-known real estate investing apps, suspended redemptions from its mature funds “until further notice.”.

The lockup is part of why these investments can pay more than a savings account, so it isn’t automatically a problem. It becomes one when money you might need in a slow month ends up somewhere that can tell you “not yet.”.

It has been revealed that how to check: Read the redemption section of the offering documents. Then ask one blunt question: “If I wanted all of it back next month, what would happen?”.

When a client asks whether an app is a good idea, try:.

“I can’t tell you whether it’s right for you, but here are the five questions to get answered first.”.

You come across as the agent who thinks clearly about money without crossing into advice you’re not licensed to give.

Industry observers note that commission income doesn’t arrive on a schedule, so the money you can reach in a slow month matters more than the money that pays the most. Before your own dollars go into a platform, make sure your cushion lives somewhere you can actually reach. Liquidity first, then growth. Treat the app as the growth layer of your proposal, not the floor under it.

It has been revealed that the average return will always be the number they show you first. Make it the last one you trust.

Amanda Neely is a Certified Financial Planner and the CEO of Counterflow. Connect with her on LinkedIn and Substack.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Siliconangle ↗ Open Full Page

Zoom’s conversations-to-completion strategy is starting to pay off

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1412 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • has spent the better part of the past few years building products to become more than just the video company everyone used during the pandemic.
  • Total revenue grew 4.9%, but enterprise revenue rose 8.6%, its fastest pace in 13 quarters.
  • The acceleration should be viewed not as a one-quarter anomaly but as a manifestation of the strategy the organization outlined at Zoomtopia about a month ago – moving from “conversations to completion.” That strategy gives customers a reason to buy more of Zoom and builds a competitive moat wider than most investors realize.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 23:43 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

ANALYSIS by Zeus Kerravala.

Zoom Communications Inc. has spent the better part of the past few years building products to become more than just the video company everyone used during the pandemic. Its fiscal third-quarter results, posted Monday, highlighted the strategy is working, though more work remains.

Total revenue grew 4.9%, but enterprise revenue rose 8.6%, its fastest pace in 13 quarters. Zoom raised its full-year outlook and unveiled its first quarterly dividend of 25 cents per share.

The acceleration should be viewed not as a one-quarter anomaly but as a manifestation of the strategy the organization outlined at Zoomtopia about a month ago – moving from “conversations to completion.” That strategy gives customers a reason to buy more of Zoom and builds a competitive moat wider than most investors realize.

The concept of conversations to completion has enough merit that Microsoft used those exact words at its recent Ignite 2026 event. In fact, it held an entire session on the topic. Though having an 800-pound gorilla like Microsoft jump on a trend might seem threatening, Zoom has a significant lead and can use Microsoft’s marketing to add momentum to its current tailwind.

In a recent development, nearly all work starts with a conversation: a meeting, a call, a chat thread or a customer interaction. Then everyone leaves, and the real work begins: updating the customer record, writing the follow-up and scheduling the next step. Collaboration vendors have always owned the first step, leaving the second to someone else.

Recent findings suggest that zoom wants both. “We’d like to leverage AI to transform our business from a conversation-centric vendor to a system of completions,” Chief Executive Eric Yuan stated on the earnings call. He later put it more plainly: “Conversation is step 1. Step 2, AI will take over.”.

AI agents are swiftly becoming a commodity, and so are the models behind them. What is scarce is context, the knowledge of what was decided, by whom, and why. Zoom sits on the richest source of it in most companies: what people actually said to one another and to customers.

It has been revealed that “Any agent without context really cannot get work done,” Yuan noted. That’s why the unified context layer Zoom showcased at Zoomtopia is central to the story. It links conversations to chats, documents and third-party systems, ensuring people and agents work from the same information.

My Notes, the manufacturer’s AI note-taker, extends that reach to third-party and in-person conversations. Yuan said it is nearing 2 million monthly active users, with one financial services firm rolling it out to 80,000 wealth advisers. Chief Financial Officer Michelle Chang added that online customers using My Notes have been associated with a 50% reduction in churn.

That is what will create a deeper competitive moat for Zoom. The more context a customer stores with Zoom, the more useful its agents become and the harder it is to leave. Zoom’s moat is not the meeting. Think of it as the memory of the meeting.

Recent findings suggest that A context layer is only as good as the number of conversations it ingests, and this is where Zoom’s breadth of platforms matters. Meetings, phone, chat, contact center and now sales intelligence all feed into the same foundation, and each product gets smarter from the others.

Industry observers note that customers are consolidating. DSI Systems is replacing five separate products with Zoom. SolarWinds expanded its Zoom licenses while “recalibrating its Microsoft package,” according to Yuan. Enterprise net dollar expansion returned to 100%, its highest level in 11 quarters. “Strong RPO growth reflects our continued success in landing larger, longer-term multiproduct platform deals, demonstrating growing demand for our AI-first platform,” Chang stated.

Customer experience is where completion gets paid for. Zoom CX recurring revenue grew in the high double digits for the seventh straight quarter, and all 10 of its largest CX deals included paid AI. More telling, Zoom said at Zoomtopia that 90% of its top 100 CX deals in the first half were with customers new to Zoom. Contact center is no longer a cross-sell. It is a front door.

Chang described the differentiation as “the ability to think about customer experience in a whole and fresh newly introduced way.” Specifically, she said, “to be able to seamlessly hand off from virtual agents to agents assisted with AI is a massive winner for us.” AI-native startups have the virtual agent but not the human side. Legacy contact center vendors have the humans but not the pace of innovation. Zoom has both on one platform.

It has been revealed that there is also an economic moat. Zoom runs most of its AI workload on its own small models and saves the expensive frontier models for harder tasks. “I fundamentally believe no single model can satisfy everything,” Yuan noted. Gross margin rose even as AI usage grew, a feat that a point product reselling another manufacturer’s tokens cannot easily match.

The quarter was strong, but analyst questions revealed several concerns.

Some will read the dividend as a sign of maturity. With more than $7 billion in cash and free cash flow margins above 40%, I see a organization that can fund innovation and return capital at the same time.

Recent findings suggest that although these issues came up during the call, most of the investment community remains positive about Zoom. In his note, Arun Bhatia of William Blair wrote, “Churn and downsell rates are becoming more favorable, AI usage and monetization are increasing, and adoption of new products such as Phone and Zoom CX is strong. We are encouraged by these trends and see potential for a growth uptick in the future.”.

Zoom’s headline growth resembles that of a mature software vendor, but the firm is in transition, so it’s crucial to look beyond the numbers. The underlying enterprise business is built to be a platform that uses context to drive customers toward more products and longer commitments. Investors should watch enterprise growth, net expansion and CX AI attach rates rather than the top line.

For information technology and business leaders, the lesson extends beyond Zoom. Conversation data is a strategic asset, so decide deliberately where it lives and which agents can act on it. Insist on openness so that context can feed the tools you choose. Start where completion is easy to measure, in the contact center and in sales.

It has been revealed that that is where Zoom is proving that the conversation was never the product. The outcome is.

#213845. Compass follows through on Reffkin’s threat, sues 15 MLSs

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1212 w)

General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

Compass follows through on Reffkin’s threat, sues 15 MLSs

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The brokerage giant declared Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states.
  • Several weeks ago at an industry conference, Compass International Holdings CEO Robert Reffkin threatened to sue MLSs that wouldn’t change their rules.
  • The company confirmed Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states, accusing the organizations of illegally restricting how agents can publicly market homes outside their systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The brokerage giant declared Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states.

Several weeks ago at an industry conference, Compass International Holdings CEO Robert Reffkin threatened to sue MLSs that wouldn’t change their rules. Now, the brokerage giant is taking another 15 of them to federal court.

The company confirmed Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states, accusing the organizations of illegally restricting how agents can publicly market homes outside their systems. Compass alleges that the MLSs unlawfully fine agents for publicly marketing listings outside the MLS, with penalties it says can reach $15,000.

Sources indicate that the announcement marks a major escalation in a fight that has been building since September, fueled by demand letters, legal threats and increasingly pointed public messaging from Compass execs. Eight of the 15 MLSs targeted Thursday are already suing Compass in two separate federal cases, adding another layer to an increasingly complicated legal battle.

A Compass spokesperson described the latest lawsuits to Inman as a follow-through on Reffkin’s warnings at the Council of Multiple Listing Services’ annual conference in Fort Lauderdale in late September, noting that some MLS organizations had filed their own lawsuits before Compass took legal action.

The lawsuits target six MLSs in California, three in North Carolina and six others across the country.

At the center of the lawsuits are MLS rules that require agents to submit listings to the MLS once they begin publicly marketing a property.

Sellers can generally keep their homes off the MLS through an office-exclusive arrangement. But advertising a property on a brokerage website, social media or other public channels typically triggers a requirement to share the listing with the MLS.

Compass argues that those rules unfairly limit competition and prevent agents from offering alternative marketing strategies, even when homeowners want to advertise their properties outside the MLS first.

It has been revealed that “Only the law and the homeowner should tell agents how to market a home, and the MLS is neither the law nor the homeowner,” a Compass spokesperson said in a statement shared with Inman. “Agents should be free to compete on the marketing strategies they offer.”.

The brokerage also rejected warnings from MLS leaders that allowing public marketing without requiring listings to be shared through the MLS would harm buyers, sellers or competing agents.

In a recent development, compass pointed to seven of the nation’s 25 largest MLSs that it said already allow agents to publicly market office-exclusive listings without fines. Those MLSs cover approximately 340,000 agents across 12 states, according to the organization.

“If what we are asking for is so bad, why has it worked for years in nearly 30 percent of the country?” the spokesperson said.

MLS leaders counter that their rules are intended to ensure that publicly marketed homes are available to other brokers and their buyers. They argue that agents who benefit from access to shared MLS listings should also contribute their own publicly marketed properties.

California Regional MLS CEO Art Carter, who spent months negotiating with Reffkin before the dispute reached federal court, emphasized that point in a recent interview with Inman.

“At some point, you’ve got to say, this is a cooperative,” Carter said.

Carter also warned that withholding listings from MLS databases could leave appraisers and lenders with incomplete information about home sales, making it harder to determine accurate property values.

It has been revealed that the new complaints largely echo arguments Compass made in its Oct. 16 antitrust lawsuit against CRMLS, accusing MLS organizations of restricting competition through their listing rules. In the complaints filed Thursday against MLSs, Compass seeks triple damages and court orders blocking enforcement of the challenged rules.

On Sept. 8, Compass attorneys sent California Regional MLS a demand letter calling on the organization to stop fining agents for publicly marketing office-exclusive listings. The brokerage gave CRMLS until Oct. 6 to comply, warning that it was prepared to spend millions of dollars on litigation if its demands weren’t met.

Similar letters went to other MLS organizations across the country.

According to recent reports, on Sept. 23, Compass International Holdings sent a separate letter demanding that MLS organizations stop sharing its agents’ production and listing data with third-party companies that help competing brokerages recruit agents. The letter specifically identified vendors Courted, BrokerMetrics and Brokerkit as examples of companies using MLS data for recruiting.

Sources indicate that compass argued that information provided to MLS organizations for real estate transactions shouldn’t be used to help competitors recruit its agents. It sought greater control over how that data was distributed, including the ability to exclude information associated with its brokerage brands from feeds used by recruiting companies.

Industry experts who recently spoke to Inman questioned parts of Compass’ argument, noting that MLS data serves purposes beyond recruiting and that access is often governed by agreements with brokerages and technology vendors.

Compass later raised the problem in its October antitrust lawsuit against CRMLS, alleging it lost millions of dollars in commissions after agents were recruited away using data the MLS allegedly sold to competing brokerages.

On Sept. 30, Reffkin took his fight over private listings directly to MLS executives at the Council of Multiple Listing Services’ annual conference in Fort Lauderdale. During a contentious session that drew pushback from attendees, Reffkin warned that Compass would begin filing antitrust lawsuits in mid-October against MLSs that continued fining agents for publicly marketing office-exclusive listings.

Photo by Michael Roberts of AJ Canaria Creative Services.

He mentioned Compass wanted to display listings on its own website without agents facing penalties, while some MLS executives questioned whether the firm’s demands went further and could undermine cooperation.

According to recent reports, the dispute reached federal court Oct. 5, when CRMLS sued Compass. Compass filed its own antitrust complaint against CRMLS on Oct. 16.

Amid the escalations, tensions and litigation in recent weeks, MLS organizations have also begun raising money to defend their rules in court. CRMLS announced plans for an MLS Cooperation Legal Defense Fund on Sept. 30, while CMLS subsequently announced a separate legal action fund to be run by an independent nonprofit.

In an Oct. 27 interview with Inman, CMLS CEO Jessica Edgerton remarked the organization had received preliminary financial commitments and was developing a process for reviewing requests for assistance.

Recent findings suggest that the growing dispute has also coincided with changes to how Compass employees participate in industry leadership. On Nov. 9, Inman broke the news that Compass International Holdings had adopted a policy restricting salaried employees from serving in Realtor association leadership positions. The directive came after brokerage managers and other employees were instructed to step down from association leadership roles, including positions some had spent years working toward.

According to recent reports, compass confirmed the policy change, saying it was extending a similar approach previously adopted by Anywhere Real Estate, which merged with Compass earlier this year. The company did not clarify whether exceptions were permitted or whether the restrictions also applied to MLS boards and committees.

Below is one of the 15 federal antitrust complaints filed by Compass against MLS organizations on Thursday. The lawsuits make similar legal arguments challenging restrictions on publicly marketing listings outside the MLS.

Recent findings suggest that charles Hoskinson, founder of Cardano (ADA), has tried to clear the air regarding the utility of the cryptocurrency. This comes as ADA has fallen more than 95% from its all-time high.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson responded to frustrated Cardano community members who are disappointed by the blockchain’s pace of development and inability to rebound from the current slump.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 21, Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson took to X to counter criticism about the current state of Cardano.

The exchange was triggered by a joke made by an X user stating that Grand Theft Auto 6 came out before a working Cardano blockchain.

Hoskinson replied to the comment, saying: “Cardano works.”.

Later, Hoskinson addressed the poor price performance of the cryptocurrency and explained that price doesn’t always reflect the capabilities of blockchain networks.

“Yeah. Price doesn't equal utility. Is Solana 75 percent less capable than it's all time high? It's an infinitely better product today for many more people. And so it is for Cardano,” he remarked.

What this means is that even if the value of a blockchain network's native cryptocurrency is dropping, the technology can still advance.

An X user, however, contested his comparison with Solana, stating that Cardano hasn’t been able to retake its previous all-time high even after years of development.

This drew an increasingly irritated response from Hoskinson.

“So every single thing a f****** scam? Everything they do failed? I’m so tired of you people,” said the Cardano founder.

This recent statement by Hoskinson comes as Cardano (ADA) remains one of the worst-performing major cryptocurrencies in the current market downturn.

According to recent reports, as per CoinGlass data, ADA is presently trading at around $0.14. The cryptocurrency is down by about 57% since the beginning of 2026.

It has lost a whopping 95.4% of its value from its all-time high of $3.09, set in September 2021.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 21, ADA briefly dipped toward $0.13. This came as another sell-off hit the broader crypto market.

Cardano has been in a steady decline, leading to criticism regarding its adoption, activity in its ecosystem and ability to compete with the likes of Ethereum and Solana.

Nonetheless, Charles Hoskinson has maintained that short-term market performance should not be conflated with the progress of blockchain technology over the long run.

Earlier this month, the Cardano founder tried to reassure frustrated ADA holders and tell them that things would eventually get better.

“It's all going to be ok. Everyone will be happy next year after all this madness, hate and idiocy,” said Hoskinson in a previous X post.

U.S. Home Prices Ticked Up 0.14% in October

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (603 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • home prices ticked up 0.14% month over month in October on a seasonally adjusted basis.
  • Prices rose 3.5% from a year earlier in October, the smallest increase since May 2026.
  • This is according to the Redfin Home Price Index (RHPI), which uses the repeat-sales pricing method to calculate seasonally adjusted changes in single-family home prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that U.S. home prices ticked up 0.14% month over month in October on a seasonally adjusted basis. That is the smallest increase in six months.

Prices rose 3.5% from a year earlier in October, the smallest increase since May 2026. Annual price growth has slowed for three straight months.

This is according to the Redfin Home Price Index (RHPI), which uses the repeat-sales pricing method to calculate seasonally adjusted changes in single-family home prices. The RHPI measures how sale prices of homes have changed since their previous sale—similar to the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices—but is reported about a month earlier. October data covers the three months ending October 31, 2026. Read the full RHPI methodology here.

It has been revealed that home prices continued to rise in October, but at a slower pace. Buyers gained more negotiating power than at any point in Redfin’s records, which date back to 2013. Only three of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas tracked by us were seller’s markets in October.

However, a buyer’s market doesn’t necessarily signal strong buyer’s demand. “Mortgage rates are not that volatile right now, but they’re still higher than they used to be. That’s holding back demand and putting some downward pressure on prices, which have started to fall in many parts of the country,” said Chen Zhao, Redfin’s head of economics research. “On a national level, we don’t think prices will fall very much.”.

There’s also more supply available now, but sellers are not willing to cut prices deeply. “Many sellers are still anchored to the prices they’ve seen over the past few years, and because few sellers are under pressure to sell, that puts a floor under prices,” noted Zhao.

Redfin tracks different types of home price trends. While our weekly and monthly housing market reports use the median home-sale price, which has recently shown a decline, the RHPI looks at repeat-sales prices of the same properties over time. It provides that isolates true underlying price appreciation rather than shifts in the types of homes selling, but because this is three-month moving average, it is also a slightly more “backward-looking view” according to Zhao.

Home prices rose in 30 of the 50 major U.S. metros month over month in October.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest increase was in Miami, where home prices rose 1.5% month over month on a seasonally adjusted basis. It’s followed by Montgomery County, PA (1.2%), Chicago (1.1%), Pittsburgh (1.0%) and Cincinnati (0.9%).

On a year-over-year basis, prices rose most in San Francisco, up 12.7%. It’s followed by Miami (11.3%), Chicago (9.5%), West Palm Beach (8.9%) and Philadelphia (8.5%).

The biggest price decline was in Seattle (-1.2% month over month). Next come Riverside (-0.7%), Detroit (-0.6%), Las Vegas (-0.6%) and Washington, DC (-0.5%).

Sources indicate that prices declined year over year in six major metros, four in Texas plus Seattle and Phoenix. San Antonio had the biggest drop (-3.0%), followed by Seattle (-2.1%), Dallas (-1.3%) and Austin (-1.1%). Houston (-0.2%) and Phoenix (-0.2%) also declined.

This report is part of Redfin’s monthly Home Price Index series. See all past reports and explore the latest data in the Redfin Data Center.

XRP has closed December in the red in eight of the past 13 years. In December of 2021, 2022 and 2025, the token lost 17%, 16.9% and 14.8%, respectively, and in December 2024, it gained 6.94%.

In 2020, XRP's December drop came as the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission sued Ripple on Dec. 22, 2020. The token lost 66.5% that month, and in January 2021, it gained 122.1%.

Industry observers note that in 2025, XRP's December drop came after the token set its all-time high of $3.65 on July 18, 2025. XRP lost 13.8% in November 2025 and 14.8% in December, and in January 2026, it fell another 10.6%.

Recent findings suggest that so far in 2026, XRP has lost value in seven of 11 months. The token's biggest monthly drops this year came in June and November, when it lost 22.1% and 25.4%, respectively, according to CryptoRank. Its best month was August, with a 30% gain.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 17, U.S. spot XRP ETFs had $1.08 billion in assets, according to SoSoValue. Since the start of November, the funds have lost about $26 million to outflows, and $19.13 million of that amount left in the week ending Nov. 13. Ripple's next monthly escrow release of 1 billion XRP is scheduled for Dec. 1.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse also commented on the sell-off on CNBC on Nov. 19. "What happens is you've got risk-on assets and people are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market, crypto included — Bitcoin, XRP — and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Anthropic IPO. What we saw after the SpaceX IPO was a rally in the crypto markets. I think you'll see that happen here as well," he said.

XRP's November drop took the token to its lowest level in two years, according to TradingView data.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Formal verification startup Sequent Inc.
  • According to recent reports, founded in London in January, Sequent offers a platform that uses artificial intelligence to find mathematical proofs that code obeys the safety rules its engineers set.
  • Curve also figures in how Sequent got started.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 02:00 EST / NOVEMBER 25 2026.

Formal verification startup Sequent Inc. today announced that it has raised $2.2 million in new funding to take its Alan proof platform out of early access.

According to recent reports, founded in London in January, Sequent offers a platform that uses artificial intelligence to find mathematical proofs that code obeys the safety rules its engineers set. Decentralized exchange Curve Finance is its first paying customer.

Curve also figures in how Sequent got started. Chief Executive Charles Cooper, who leads development of Vyper, one of the two main programming languages for Ethereum, inadvertently introduced a flaw into the Vyper compiler in 2021. Though the bug was fixed within months, programs already running on the blockchain could not be updated, leaving older Curve pools and other projects exposed when attackers used the flaw to take more than $50 million in July 2023.

Sources indicate that following the incident, Ramana Kumar, now Sequent’s chief technology officer and formerly an AI safety researcher at Google DeepMind, offered to help prove the Vyper compiler correct. Kumar co-created CakeML, a compiler proved correct all the way down to the instructions a computer runs.

Cooper believes the lesson reaches far beyond crypto, saying that “smart contracts taught us that anything that can be exploited will be.” Banks, governments and companies running older systems have relied on keeping their code private, according to Cooper, who said AI-powered cyberattacks are now eroding that protection.

Alan works today on Vyper smart contracts, with support for Solidity and Solana in development and general software in Rust, C, TypeScript and Python to follow.

It has been revealed that for now, engineers using Alan write rules for their code such as “no user can withdraw more than their balance” in plain language, and the job of finding a mathematical proof is handed to AI. Nothing the AI comes up with is taken on trust, as each proof has to get through HOL4, a checker Kumar has helped build for more than a decade.

It has been revealed that for two-coin StableSwap pools holding standard tokens, Alan was used to prove that no user can take more than a set limit from depositors, whatever they do and in whatever order. The work also found minor accounting and rounding errors, none of which breached the limit. The founders are now proving the Vyper compiler itself, since the Curve proof does not cover the compiler where the 2021 flaw sat.

Recent findings suggest that along with AI computing costs, the funding will pay for engineering, sales and marketing hires. Subscriptions to Alan start at $99 a month for individuals, with auditor prepares priced at $200 a month and team plans starting at $500 a month.

Recent findings suggest that frachtis and Metaplanet Holdings OÜ co-led the pre-seed round. Metaplanet is the investment firm of Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn, who led Anthropic PBC’s Series A round in 2021. According to Frachtis founder Xavier Meegan, crypto is the right place to start, with “billions already at risk.”.

  • The Blockstream CEO addressed the glitch on X on Saturday in a reply to a post that tracked large sell orders hitting Kraken's BTC/CAD order book at regular intervals throughout the night.

Blockstream CEO Adam Back has explained the overnight sell-off on Kraken's Canadian-dollar markets that sent the exchange's BTC/CAD pair to C$24,250, or roughly $17,000, on Saturday morning, and noted that the drop started with the exchange's local USD/CAD market maker.

The Blockstream CEO addressed the glitch on X on Saturday in a reply to a post that tracked large sell orders hitting Kraken's BTC/CAD order book at regular intervals throughout the night.

The $17,000 figure is based on the Bank of Canada's Friday rate of C$1.4325 per U.S. dollar. Kraken's BTC/CAD pair printed the C$24,250 low on Saturday morning, according to TradingView data.

"No, the reason was USDCAD Kraken local spot FX market-maker ran out of money, as it has depegged away from market rate 1.434," Back replied.

In the same post, the Blockstream CEO said that it was "more accurate to say you could buy CAD discounted.".

In a recent development, later, another X user argued that the Canadian dollar was in fact overvalued on Kraken during the sell-off, since anyone who held CAD could buy anything at a discount. Back agreed with the correction.

Sources indicate that "You are right. BTCUSD normal price, USDCAD CAD mispriced, like a shortage of CAD bid the price up," Back wrote.

On Sunday, the Blockstream CEO described the whole chain of events in two more posts on X.

Recent findings suggest that according to Back, if the USD/CAD market maker failed, there were few buyers of BTC in Canadian dollars, and so the BTC/CAD price fell. In his view, traders would normally close such a gap with an arbitrage trade "by selling USD to CAD to buy if it BTCCAD doesn't track BTCUSD.".

Back wrote that the drop "liquidated people" and triggered stop losses "based on a local false price.".

"And then USDCAD followed because you could buy BTC cheaply in CAD, so it became logical to buy CAD way over par to take that arb," he added.

The BTC/CAD pair recovered later on Saturday, and on Sunday, it traded at C$86,236 on Kraken, according to TradingView.

Kraken remarked in a statement that its Canadian-dollar trading pairs faced heavy selling pressure starting around 20:00 UTC on Friday, and prices on these pairs fell significantly below those on other markets.

The Kraken sell-off started on the same day that Bitcoin dropped to $59,370, its lowest level since July 2, according to CoinGlass data. On Friday, CoinGlass also recorded $1.57 billion in liquidations across the crypto market over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of that amount.

Still, the exchange mentioned that every order was processed correctly and that its security teams found no evidence of a breach or compromised accounts.

"Executed trades stand," Kraken remarked.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A co-living community in West Oakland, CA, has hit the market for the first time.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Union is a three-house, 14-bedroom compound and is listed at $2,999,995.
  • Each home is separately deeded as a condo within the greater compound.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A co-living community in West Oakland, CA, has hit the market for the first time.

Recent findings suggest that the Union is a three-house, 14-bedroom compound and is listed at $2,999,995. That’s the asking price for all three homes. If purchased separately by friends, multigenerational families, or any other buyers who want to live side by side, the starting price is $899,000 for the smallest of the three homes, which has five bedrooms and four bathrooms.

Each home is separately deeded as a condo within the greater compound.

This lot has been zoned RM-3, or Mixed Housing Type Residential–3, which allows for multiple single-family homes on a single lot. This setup is permissible due to changes in California law allowing for higher-density housing in residential areas.

This project started in 2019 when a startup called Open Door bought the 7,535-square-foot empty lot and tasked Matt Baran of Baran Studio Architecture with creating a co-living space.

They asked: “What if we design something that can be beautiful design and work with the upcoming state laws that allow for increased density in neighborhoods and works well for community living?” states listing agent Max Nelson, who specializes in co-living sales through the platform Live Near Friends.

The end result was a rent-by-the-room community where residents enjoyed shared amenities, including a backyard fire pit, co-working space, and rooftop deck with views of downtown Oakland.

The design process balanced group-friendly amenities with the look and feel of the neighborhood, which is filled with mostly Victorian homes.

Nelson claims that the architects asked, “How do we create a modern house without making it look like it doesn't fit?”.

Industry observers note that the design included bay windows that jut from the homes, mirroring the style of a classic Victorian. Having three separate homes rather than one huge building also matched the aesthetic of the area, as did the incorporation of tall, narrow windows.

Much of the rest of the design leans more modern, especially the efficient energy systems. The homes rely on shared solar panels, greatly reducing energy bills. Everything is electric—there is no reliance on gas. Each room has its own fan coils to create customized comfort.

“It’s a super efficient, well-done system,” notes Nelson.

Because The Union was designed for co-living, some of the best features are the shared spaces and the flow among the three homes.

Sources indicate that the property fronting the street, 1514, has the smaller price tag at $899,000 and offers 1,919 square feet of living space, including five bedrooms and four bathrooms. A skybridge connects it with the back two condos, positioned side by side like a duplex and sharing a common wall.

The larger of the back condos, 1510, is listed at $1,049,500 and sits slightly larger at 2,033 square feet, again with five bedrooms and four bathrooms. Connected is 1512, also offered at $1,049,500 with 2,015 square feet, including four bedrooms and four bathrooms.

Above these two condos is the roof area, which houses the solar panels as well as the communal deck with AstroTurf and several seating areas.

In a recent development, it all adds up to a highly functional, thoughtfully designed compound that meets the needs of communal living. It offers both shared spaces as well as smaller decks, outdoor seating nooks, and private spaces for solo or one-on-one time with another—because shared living works best when people have the freedom to come together or enjoy time apart.

#213836. Your ‘just sold’ posts are missing the best part of the story

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1147 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

Your ‘just sold’ posts are missing the best part of the story

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1147 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Use ChatGPT Voice and footage you already have, plus this free Canva template, to tell the story behind the sale.
  • I’ve always found it interesting how much time and energy we put into selling a home, only to reduce the entire experience to a “just sold” graphic once the transaction closes.
  • We spend weeks, sometimes months, developing a marketing strategy, communicating with sellers, negotiating with buyers and navigating challenges along the way, but so little of that work makes it into the content we share afterward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turn closings into case studies. Use ChatGPT Voice and footage you already have, plus this free Canva template, to tell the story behind the sale.

I’ve always found it interesting how much time and energy we put into selling a home, only to reduce the entire experience to a “just sold” graphic once the transaction closes.

We spend weeks, sometimes months, developing a marketing strategy, communicating with sellers, negotiating with buyers and navigating challenges along the way, but so little of that work makes it into the content we share afterward.

Industry observers note that I don’t think there’s anything wrong with celebrating a closing. But I’ve always felt that the story behind the sale is often more interesting than the sale itself, especially when you consider what a prospective client is trying to figure out when deciding who to hire.

Most sellers probably assume any experienced agent can put their home on the market. What they don’t necessarily know is how that agent approaches marketing, how much effort they’ll put into a listing or how they’ll respond when something doesn’t go according to proposal. Those are difficult things to communicate in a listing presentation when every agent is promising some version of the same thing.

For years, I’ve tried to give people a better understanding of our work by creating case studies of the homes we’ve sold. Initially, that meant compiling listing footage into a Reel with a longer caption explaining the transaction. More recently, I’ve been experimenting with carousels that tell those stories across multiple slides using footage we already created to market the property.

What I like about this approach is that people can see what working with us might actually look like, rather than simply taking our word for it.

According to recent reports, we recently sold a property in San Pedro where we hosted nine open houses, mailed 500 postcards, ran digital advertising and created a video that generated more than 1.5 million organic views. We found a buyer and opened escrow, but shortly before closing, that buyer backed out, and we had to start again.

A post shared by KRYS BENYAMEIN | LA & OC Real Estate Agent (@krysbenyamein).

We eventually found another buyer and successfully closed, but when we shared the case study, we didn’t lead with the sale price or how much marketing we’d done. We opened with, “Imagine finally selling your house. Then the buyer backs out right before closing.”.

In a recent development, I liked that opening because it put the reader in the seller’s position. Most homeowners can imagine how frustrating that experience would be, and it naturally creates curiosity about what happened next. From there, we explained how we responded, got the property back in front of buyers, and ultimately closed.

We’ve used the same approach to tell different stories, including a transaction in Hesperia, California, where we coordinated a sale for sellers who had moved out of state, and a humorous carousel about a San Diego transaction that generated 15,741 views.

A post shared by KRYS BENYAMEIN | LA & OC Real Estate Agent (@krysbenyamein).

Industry observers note that not every transaction needs an extraordinary twist. Sometimes the interesting part is a problem you solved, a decision you made, or the work that went into making the experience easier for your client. The challenge is recognizing those moments and figuring out how to communicate them.

The storytelling portion generally takes me about 15 minutes, although gathering information and designing the finished post take additional time.

Before writing, I go through the transaction and take inventory of everything we’ve done. I want to know how many open houses we hosted, how many people attended, how many postcards we mailed, how much content we published and how many views our videos generated. I’ll also look at offers received and anything else that helps explain how the sale unfolded.

In a recent development, this has made me more conscious of documenting our work as we’re doing it. It’s difficult to communicate the effort behind a sale if you can’t remember the specifics, and having those numbers also makes it easier to evaluate what worked.

I then gather content we’ve already created, whether that’s property videos, walkthroughs, open house footage, or photographs. Repurposing footage gives that content another life, but agents could create something similar using listing photos.

It has been revealed that once I have everything together, I open ChatGPT Voice and talk through the transaction. I’ll explain the sellers’ circumstances, our approach, the decisions we made and anything unexpected. I don’t organize my thoughts beforehand because I find it more helpful to get everything out and work through the story conversationally.

What I’ve found particularly useful is having ChatGPT ask follow-up questions to identify the most compelling angle. Sometimes what I initially find interesting isn’t what another homeowner would care about, and that back-and-forth helps me consider their perspective.

It has been revealed that once we’ve found the angle, we work on the writing, particularly the opening two slides because Instagram can serve both to your audience. Lately, I’ve preferred carousels with moving video backgrounds, but we’ve also created Reels and experimented with humor. I’ve shared an editable version of our Canva template for anyone who wants to try the format.

If you want to try this with one of your transactions, open ChatGPT Voice and use this prompt:.

In a recent development, “Interview me about [Address] I recently closed. Ask me one question at a time about the seller’s goals, our marketing strategy, the decisions we made, challenges we encountered and the outcome. Help me identify the most compelling part of the story and why another homeowner would care. Once we’ve found the angle, help me write a seven-slide Instagram carousel with a strong opening and a natural narrative. Use specific details and results, avoid generic sales language, and don’t invent anything.”.

We’ve also been sharing these case studies in emails to our database, giving us another opportunity to demonstrate our experience to homeowners and agents who may eventually refer us business.

According to recent reports, if you’ve been in the business for any length of time, you probably have dozens of transactions worth revisiting, with interesting stories buried in them. You don’t need a newly introduced closing every week to share those experiences, and you don’t need to make every transaction sound more dramatic than it was.

Sources indicate that there’s tremendous value in helping people understand the work we do, particularly when so much happens behind the scenes. If we’re already investing all this time and effort into helping our clients, it seems like a missed opportunity not to share more of it.

Use this FREE Canva template to replicate these results.

Krys Benyamein is a Realtor with Allstars Realty in Southern California. Get connected on Instagram or LinkedIn.

Sources indicate that TEMPE, Ariz., Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GoDaddy, the world's largest domain registrar, recently introduced GoDaddy Airo AI Builder, an agentic operating system for small businesses.

In a recent development, professionals in the beauty industry, including salon owners, beauticians and nail technicians, can use simple voice or text conversations to create a professional online presence. By describing what they need, they can ask Airo to build a customized website and web app in minutes, then refine the experience with natural conversation prompts or direct edits, with no coding needed.

Running a beauty business means focusing on clients while also juggling to keep services, photos, pricing and business information up to date. Airo is designed to simplify that work, with fast results and minimal prompting. Owners can ask Airo to build an initial website and make updates while working with a client or between appointments.

In a recent development, "Whether running a salon, spa or independent beauty business, entrepreneurs need tools that help them showcase what makes their business unique, attract fresh customers and keep things running smoothly," said Selina Bieber, vice president of marketing-led growth at GoDaddy. "Airo AI Builder helps them bring their business online, connect the booking platforms they already use and manage more of their business in one place, so they can spend less time juggling tools and more time focused on their clients.".

What is the best payment processing solution for a salon that supports online bookings, client management and in-person payments?

Recent findings suggest that airo AI Builder's commerce tools help industry professionals manage appointment payments and sell retail products. They can also create product catalogs for skincare and other beauty products, with shopping cart and checkout capabilities on their website.

For in-person sales, the GoDaddy App and lineup of Smart Terminal Point of Sale (POS) devices lets owners access their existing product catalog and accept credit and debit card payments, plus Apple Pay and Google Pay, bringing online and in-person sales together. #213834. Open-weight models are the hottest thing in AI. Are they right for you?

Open-weight models are the hottest thing in AI. Are they right for you?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the first three years of the generative artificial intelligence boom, enterprise technology strategy relied on a simple rule: Select the premier frontier foundation model, route every prompt through its commercial application programming interface and pay the subscription premium for access to cutting-edge technology.
  • In a recent development, that monolithic approach is now collapsing under the weight of operational reality.
  • These models don’t necessarily provide access to their training data, source code or training methods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 10:59 EST / NOVEMBER 25 2026.

For the first three years of the generative artificial intelligence boom, enterprise technology strategy relied on a simple rule: Select the premier frontier foundation model, route every prompt through its commercial application programming interface and pay the subscription premium for access to cutting-edge technology.

In a recent development, that monolithic approach is now collapsing under the weight of operational reality. Open-weight models, AI models whose trained parameters, or “weights,” are publicly available for others to download, run, customize and fine-tune, are the overnight sensation in an industry already moving at light speed.

These models don’t necessarily provide access to their training data, source code or training methods. They also carry a variety of license types that may restrict how they can be used commercially. But they offer choice, flexibility and cost advantages that the leading-edge “frontier” models such as OpenAI Group PBC’s ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC’s Claude don’t. For information technology organizations, they can be a respite from spiraling token costs.

Industry observers note that the popularity of these models has soared as AI has matured and organizations have realized that not every use case demands the biggest and best solution. They come in various shapes and sizes, ranging from less than 1 billion to nearly 3 trillion parameters. Many are tuned for specific tasks, such as recognizing images or writing software. That gives organizations the flexibility to match the model to the job.

“Frontier intelligence is priced for the hardest problems, and most agent work isn’t hard,” mentioned Dhruv Amin, co-founder of Anything, the business name of Create Inc. and developer of an AI-powered platform for building mobile and web applications. “Companies are chartering a jet to cross the street.”.

“There are lots of tasks in customer self-service and employee self-service that need a smaller model,” noted Dheeraj Pandey, chief executive officer of DevRev Inc., maker of a unified customer support, software development and engineering platform.

DevRev created an open, vendor-neutral benchmark to measure how reliably enterprise AI agents perform in realistic organizational environments. “We get almost the same accuracy and precision on enterprise tasks, whether you use the open-weight models or the frontier models,” he said.

The ascendancy of open-weight models has been breathtaking. Vercel Inc.’s monthly AI Gateway report found that their share of observed token traffic surged from 7% last December to 56% in August and that the models held eight of the 10 busiest spots on OpenRouter Inc.’s large language model ranking in August by token volume.

Industry observers note that three-year-old OpenRouter itself turned heads in August when it sold to Stripe Inc. for an eye-popping $7.5 billion. The firm’s technology connects developers and users with hundreds of AI models from dozens of providers through a single interface.

In a recent development, in September, Nvidia Corp. paid nearly $13 billion for Hugging Face Inc., which hosts more than 3 million models. “For most enterprises, the practical path to an open-weight model — evaluate, fine-tune, quantize, deploy — runs through that hub,” wrote Zeus Kerravala, principal analyst at ZK Research, referring to Hugging Face.

It has been revealed that enterprises aren’t abandoning frontier models. Rather, they’re learning to fit the model to the problem. None of the experts SiliconANGLE contacted believes open-weight models are a threat to the significant players.

“All players can win because the market is growing and the number of places where it makes sense to deploy AI increases,” Amin said.

Cost is right now the principal driver of open-weight adoption. As AI use has evolved from question-and-response generative models to sophisticated multistep agentic workflows, inference costs have soared. Gartner Inc. predicts inference costs per agentic workflow will increase more than fivefold through 2028.

“They are rapidly starting to rival even payroll expenses,” Amin said.

By most accounts, frontier models still offer the greatest power and range of usage options. But the gap is closing. Mozilla’s September State of Open-Source AI report put the capability gap between leading open-weight models and proprietary frontier models at roughly four months, down from 18 months just two years ago.

It has been revealed that “The differences in quality are starting to be outweighed by the differences in cost,” wrote Ioana Hreninciuc, co-founder of inference platform Runware Ltd. She noted that though proprietary models still lead on top-tier reasoning, “you probably don’t need a frontier model for 80% of what you do.”.

According to recent reports, the pivot to open weights isn’t a zero-sum proposition. Low token prices can mask integration overhead, tool failures and operational risk. “Tokenomics,” or measuring, attributing and managing the cost of tokens, has become an essential information technology discipline.

It has been revealed that in a Hyper Labs Inc. survey conducted by The Harris Poll, 86% of AI leaders noted managing token expenses is as critical as containing cloud costs. More than three-quarters said they are directing routine tasks to smaller models to protect budgets, while 89% have redesigned AI initiatives after getting token shock.

“The whole world is trying to solve for tokenomics,” stated Armando Franco, senior director of cloud and platform modernization at IT services provider TEKsystems Inc.

In a recent development, experts say open-weight models are well-suited for repetitive, routine workloads. “Basically, they work best when the task is clear and it’s easy enough to check if the work was done correctly,” stated Louis Amira, CEO of Circuit & Chisel Inc., an AI infrastructure and agentic commerce startup.

Karen Panetta, an IEEE Fellow and dean of graduate education at Tufts University School of Engineering, remarked open models are flourishing as technology leaders learn to match the engine to the task.

“If a bicycle will get you there, don’t pick the expensive sports car,” she stated. “You have to ask: What problem you are trying to solve?” She asserted that for applications that don’t require 99.9% precision, organizations can achieve massive savings with compact models.

They’re also an attractive option when protecting customer data is a priority, since sensitive information never needs to leave the organization. “Customer data never, never goes into a frontier,” Scott Wallace, senior global director of solutions architecture at Digital Realty Inc., said in an interview with the Financial Times.

Sovereignty, or the ability to control and govern digital assets in line with local laws, security needs, and strategic interests, is a growing matter for organizations. A Linux Foundation survey last year found that 79% of AI leaders — and 86% in the U.S. — rate sovereignty as a strategic priority.

“What began as a specialized concern for highly regulated industries is rapidly becoming a strategic consideration for nearly every enterprise,” Paul Nashawaty, a principal analyst at theCUBE Research, wrote in a recent analysis.

Some early adopters are demonstrating impressive returns.

In a recent development, advocates point to a shrinking capability gap, too, with some open-weight models nipping at the heels of the frontier alternatives. Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co., Ltd.’s 2.8 trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s 2.4 trillion-parameter Qwen3.8-Max nearly match closed models on coding benchmarks, according to Stanford University’s Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence Institute.

According to recent reports, an agent built by Tenzai Inc. recently captured the top spot on HackerOne’s leaderboard using Z.ai Inc.’s GLM 5.2, generating 30% more findings per unit of computing power than a previous baseline using a proprietary model.

“What was the frontier 18 months ago is now well-mapped territory, and open-source models are closing the gap at a fraction of the cost” wrote Runware’s Hreninciuc.

Sources indicate that though such metrics explain open models’ ascendancy, the decision to use them isn’t open-and-shut. Experts cite four common myths that can mitigate the cost efficiencies.

Industry observers note that one is the mistaken belief that open-weight models conflate with traditional open-source software and its permissive licenses. “This is a misnomer among many enterprises,” noted Dr. Dorotea Baljević, EMEA Lead for AI Advisory at technology research and advisory firm Information Services Group. “There is licensing for these models in most cases, particularly for commercial usage.”.

Although some, such as Qwen3, Mistral 3, Gemma 4 and DeepSeek V4, are covered by standard Apache or MIT licenses, terms and conditions vary. For example, Liquid AI Inc.’s open-weight models are free for commercial use only to organizations with less than $10 million in annual revenue.

“Other licenses require attribution, restrict certain application categories, or impose acceptable use policies, none of which carry a direct fee but all of which create legal exposure if ignored,” noted Bumu Technologies Inc., which does business as Nanobase.

Recent findings suggest that evaluating models for accuracy, stability and explainability also falls to the user. With thousands of open-weight models available, the costs of a bake-off between multiple candidates can add up.

Baljević suggests organizations consider whether the model will be used internally or externally, the organization’s tolerance for accuracy, strategic fit and switching costs as evaluation criteria. Performance on public benchmarks also doesn’t guarantee a model will work well with an organization’s data, workflows and language.

It has been revealed that finance leaders may look at the 80% to 90% cost advantage of open-weight tokens and assume operational expenditures will drop proportionally. But tokens are only one part of the cost equation and not necessarily even the biggest one.

Organizations that strategy to deploy models on their own infrastructure must bear the costs of integration, API development, IT infrastructure and human labor required for auditing and verification. A fraction of a cent saved on an inference call can be wiped out by the cost of a human expert spending a half-hour re-entering flawed database transactions.

Lack of visibility into how the model is operating can also produce sticker shock. A retry loop, in which an agent tries repeatedly to complete a failed task, can go on for hours or even days. The Wall Street Journal recently reported on a case in which an AI-generated out-of-office message at a San Francisco-based software manufacturer went into a loop that ultimately burned $10,000 a day in token costs.

If a cheap open-weight model fails a multi-system query or generates invalid JSON, it triggers automated retries that can consume millions of secondary tokens. The human expertise required to repair the transaction manually can erase months of token savings.

It has been revealed that “The core software engineering required to test and integrate upcoming models into the software stack is often the biggest hurdle, since not all frontier models have the same capabilities, APIs and such,” said Alex Bakker, an ISG distinguished analyst. “The frontier labs tend to maintain more consistency in their upgrade paths.”.

Using private graphics processing unit clusters eliminates external API fees, but self-hosting economics hinge on high, sustained utilization. Models that sit idle or at low usage levels consume power, create processing inefficiencies and incur costs if restarts are required.

In a recent development, cast AI Group Inc. reported last spring that the average GPU utilization was 5% across thousands of clusters it monitored. Frontier models are usually a better option in that case. “Open models can be dramatically cheaper at high utilization, while frontier APIs remain cheaper for intermittent workloads because you aren’t paying for idle capacity,” said Arun Chandrasekaran, distinguished VP analyst at Gartner.

For intermittent workloads such as batch payroll processing or seasonal financial reporting, the organization pays 100% of capital expenses, power, cooling and depreciation while hardware idles.

“On-premises hosting wins when there is high, predictable 24/7 traffic where servers are constantly busy,” remarked Debojyoti Dutta, chief AI officer at Nutanix Inc. A hosted frontier model is a better choice “with spiky or lower traffic, where paying per token with zero setup cost is cheaper than renting idle hardware.”.

When AI agents fail, the default reaction is to switch to a newer model, but benchmark data reveals that approach is usually a dead end.

Recent findings suggest that most evaluation tests give agents relatively simple tasks and judge them mainly on whether they get the right answer. But real business environments are much more complicated. Agents must gather information from different systems, connect it correctly, handle growing amounts of data, and work within security rules.

Industry observers note that this interface complexity is what usually breaks AI agents. DevRev estimates that moving an agent from clean test tools to real-world corporate use causes an 18% to 19% drop in accuracy. Upgrading the model improves performance by less than 1%.

Industry observers note that “Every time a new model comes out, you need to re-evaluate your benchmarks, your models and your fine-tuning processes,” stated Steven Yang, senior director of product management at Tanium Inc. That means better data integration is a more effective strategy than buying new models.

Though the open-weight option is viable for any tech giant, experts say the best use cases are those where control, accountability and performance are paramount. The following three factors are at least as important as cost.

According to recent reports, compliance: Regulated industries have been held back from adopting AI over data residency and confidentiality concerns. Deploying open weights within enterprise data centers or virtual private clouds reduces the need for external data egress, ensures zero training data retention and allows for total physical isolation. The models also allow inspection of internal mechanics such as log-probabilities, token confidence scores and loss landscapes.

Training datasets, model weights and inference prompts never cross borders or leave the organization’s physical perimeter. That makes it easier to comply with strict data localization laws such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act in the U.S. and the General Data Protection Regulation in Europe. Local auditing and observability also aid in compliance with regulatory frameworks like the EU AI Act, which requires detailed logging, risk assessments and explainability.

It has been revealed that but deploying on private infrastructure isn’t a cure-all. “You still have to maintain an aggressive data security posture around your processes because even open-weight models sometimes will take action trying to accomplish their tasks that could potentially violate some type of compliance rule,” stated TEKSystems’ Franco.

It has been revealed that transparency: Understanding how models arrive at an answer is critical in many scenarios, particularly those involving safety, law and finance. “Open-weight models expose the math behind their answers,” said Brian Weiss, chief technology officer at document processing platform maker Hyperscience, the business name of Hyper Labs Inc. “You can use that to hold the model accountable for accuracy.”.

In contrast, frontier APIs often obscure the equations used to generate probabilities, which are critical to assessing accuracy. Asking a model how confident it is in its answer may yield a subjective response. Open weights allow confidence scores to be scored against ground-truth outcomes for better reliability.

“People can take these models inside their organization, do some post-training and fine-tuning and have a customized model where they know the costs, where it’s sitting and what data is being sent to it,” mentioned David DeSanto, CEO of Anaconda Inc., maker of an AI development platform.

“The future is an orchestrated ensemble of bounded, transparent, governed, cost-effective models,” Weiss said. “If I find a better model for a particular task, I can swap it out because I have the framework to do that.”.

In a recent development, performance: As organizations move from the relatively simple generative AI question-and-response metaphor to sophisticated multi-agent frameworks, latency issues can compound exponentially. For example, a 500-millisecond API delay across 50 sequential reasoning steps creates 25 seconds of cumulative latency, which would render many applications useless.

Executing open-weight models directly alongside operational databases or within containerized edge pods minimizes routing hops and rate limits. Distillation, which trains smaller, specialized open models from frontier “teacher” models, is faster.

Hyperscience reported that distillation delivers up to 97% cost reduction and four times faster inference, while retaining over 95% of the original model’s performance on designated tasks. Small models are faster and considerably cheaper than frontier LLMs.

Experts say constructing a business case for open-weight models requires understanding three major sources of hidden expense.

Sources indicate that complexity tax: Reasoning can break down when open-weight models interact with complex enterprise data at scale. The “Cartesian Shortcut” refers to a phenomenon in which AI models rely on workarounds learned during training rather than demonstrating a flexible understanding of the problem they’re trying to solve.

Google LLC researchers found that the models struggled with visual reasoning problems, such as solving mazes, when the data was presented in a circular rather than a grid layout. Leading models answered 69% to 83% of the square-grid problems correctly, but their accuracy fell to below 40% when the problems appeared in circular layouts.

Industry observers note that the corollary to a business scenario is a multihop join across multiple systems. Models may “cheat” by collapsing field-level relationships into hierarchical groupings, generating massive data fabrications.

Human oversight remains critical: “For validation and rework, humans in the loop need to be taken into account on top of all the tokens you’re paying for already,” remarked TekSystems’ Franco.

Poor data quality: Foundation models can’t fix bad data, a fact that’s holding back AI adoption across the board. The Hyperscience/Harris Poll study found that 86% of IT leaders remarked dirty internal data is actively crippling GenAI performance.

Sources indicate that feeding error-strewn or outdated information into probabilistic models creates “context pollution,” the accumulation of irrelevant, redundant, outdated or contradictory information. When agents execute multistep database joins, system workflows or automated tool calls based on flawed data or ambiguous schemas, cascading errors can occur.

Recent findings suggest that sauce Labs Inc. Chief Technology Officer Anoop Tripathi recommends creating validated “golden datasets” for fine-tuning and evaluation. He also cautions architects against misapplying probabilistic AI to structured business logic. In other words, use models only where they add value and apply conventional (and cheaper) data processing to everything else.

Continuous evaluation: Selecting the right model out of thousands of open-weight alternatives requires ongoing evaluation against internal workloads rather than public leaderboards. That demands expensive MLOps, site reliability engineering and platform engineering skills.

Because new models are constantly being introduced and revised, Circuit & Chisel’s Amira recommends building custom testing harnesses that can quickly evaluate candidate models against business-relevant tasks.

Industry observers note that rather than treating open-weight adoption as an all-or-nothing choice, enterprise architects should bucket organizational tasks into distinct operational tiers. Don’t feed every problem into a token-hungry trillion-parameter model if a smaller, specialized one will do the trick.

“Organizations don’t give a heavyweight reasoning model a lightweight sorting job,” said Nutanix’s Dutta. “They divide their business workloads into tiers based on cost, speed and hardware footprint.”.

Industry observers note that lower-tier workloads such as search, embeddings and document classification work well with inexpensive, compact open-weight and small language models. Sophisticated tasks such as autonomous reasoning and restructuring large, deeply entangled legacy software systems are better suited to commercial alternatives.

Industry observers note that ISG’s Bakker believes the need for constant evaluation is the biggest impediment to open-weight adoption. “The core software engineering required to test and integrate new models into the software stack will likely be the biggest hurdle, since not all frontier models have the same capabilities and APIs,” he said. “The frontier labs tend to maintain more consistency in their upgrade paths.”.

Enterprise IT organizations must develop expertise in local model execution, containerized execution sandboxes and agent harness orchestration. Managing AI and agents safely “is, in the near future, going to be as vital an indigenous knowledge as how to upgrade Windows,” stated Gordon Allott, founder and CEO of private infrastructure provider nFOX Lab.

In a recent development, the shift toward open-weight models represents a permanent maturation of enterprise IT from experimentation to disciplined financial and architectural management. Success is no longer about raw model parameter size or benchmark ranking, but matching the model to the task. That’s a discipline that was barely on the roadmap a year ago.

According to recent reports, at the start of the year, there was no way enterprises were going to touch open-weight models, Brad Maltz, head of AI factory solutions at Dell Technologies Inc., mentioned in a November interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE’s streaming media platform. “People were pretty wrong about that. I think the open-weight movement is the future.”.

In the final stretch of 2026, some XRP Ledger protocol features await mainnet activation, with validator support and amendment voting as the final steps to bring latest functionality to the XRPL network.

In light of this, three amendments are racing against the 2026 calendar, with only a few votes left to reach a majority and enter the two-week activation period. These include SingleAssetVault, LendingProtocol and confidential transfers.

All three remain below the required validator approval threshold of over 80% support, making the final weeks of the year increasingly important for their activation prospects.

With about five weeks left in 2026, activation remains possible this year, but additional validator support for each amendment must arrive soon enough and be sustained to complete the required two-week activation window.

According to recent reports, the lending protocol allows on-chain fixed-term, uncollateralized loans from pooled funds in a Single Asset Vault. There are two amendments: LendingProtocolV1_1 and the original Lending Protocol amendment.

The focus is on LendingProtocolV1_1, which extends the Lending Protocol and SingleAssetVault amendments with a upcoming closed-ended vault and cash-basis accounting. With the amendment, new loan brokers can only be created against closed-ended vaults.

Sources indicate that lendingProtocolV1_1 has reached 70.59% support with 24 out of 34 validators voting yes, according to XRPScan data. It needs 28 votes to reach a majority, or more than 80% of 34 votes, meaning it has just four votes left.

Industry observers note that A major privacy amendment for the XRP Ledger, confidential transfers, has 64.71% support and 22 of 34 validators voting yes. Confidential transfers, which rely on advanced cryptography (EC-ElGamal and ZKPs), offer institutional-grade privacy for Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTs) and need six more yes votes to enter the activation window.

SingleAssetVault creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. It has gained 73.53% support so far with 25 out of 34 validators voting in favor. Reaching more than 80% of 34 votes requires 28 votes; thus, three votes remain for it to enter the activation window.
